asked: Locked-off camera, framing holds. The six masked men walk slowly toward the camera in step, an unhurried stride, guns resting upright on their shoulders. Their heads nod gently with each step. Long shadows slide forward over the cobbles. Every parked car stays parked and unchanged; the street stays empty behind them. Masks, gloves and suits stay exactly as they are. SFX: shoes on cobbles in a steady rhythm. Ambient noise: a quiet early-morning street.

Locked-off camera, framing holds. The man in front takes two firm steps toward the camera, gun held straight up at the ceiling. The gang behind him follows at a walk. The glass fragments in the air drift down and settle on the marble. The bystanders keep crouching and shielding themselves. Dust turns slowly in the sunlight. Masks stay exactly as they are. SFX: tinkling glass landing, heavy footsteps. Ambient noise: a large echoing hall.

Locked-off camera at kerb height, framing holds. The black sedan finishes its sideways skid, rocks once on its springs and stops in place. Grey tyre smoke drifts and thins; the loose oranges roll a little and settle. The man on the running board grips the door frame and nods his shoulders on a steady beat. Same car, same street, masks unchanged, gloves on, nothing enters the frame. SFX: tyre screech dying out, a wooden crate thud, engine idle. No voices.

Locked-off camera, framing holds. The policeman keeps the earpiece to his ear and jabs his free arm toward the road twice on the beat, shouting with his whole body. The black 1920s roadster rolls slowly forward to the right, staying fully in frame, its spoked wheels turning and throwing puddle spray that falls back to the cobbles. The masked driver keeps both gloved hands on the wheel; his mask keeps its exact shape. Rain falls steadily. Audio: heavy rain, an old engine revving, water splashing, a call-box bell ringing; no voices.

Locked-off camera, no camera movement. The six masked men round the iron press perform together like a stadium act in a cellar. On the first beat all six punch their fists up at the low ceiling in unison. On the next they bounce at the knees, shoulders shrugging, heads nodding hard. Then the two in the middle slam both gloves flat on top of the press while the others point down at it with both hands, mock-outraged. Then all six throw both arms up, palms raised, and pump them on every beat. Nobody leaves their place. Stamps and cloth rustle.

Locked-off camera, no camera movement. The man in the green balaclava leans on the bar and performs straight into the lens from the first instant. First beat: his raised thumb jerks back over his shoulder at the barman, twice, sharp. Next beat: his lower gloved hand chops flat on the bar top, once per beat, like a metronome. Next: both palms open wide in an exaggerated shrug, head tilted. Then he counts off three gloved fingers close to the lens, head nodding on each. Behind him the barman calmly keeps pouring water from the tin jug into the bottle. Sound: palm thumps on wood. No speech.

Locked-off camera, framing holds. Seated behind the microphone, the masked man raps with his body: he jabs his gloved finger at the lens on each beat, four times, while his other fist pumps in time and his head nods steadily under the fedora. On the wall behind him his horned shadow repeats every movement exactly, the horns staying in place. Mask, hat and gloves unchanged; the microphone and valves stay still. SFX: a steady boom-bap beat, a soft valve hum, no voices.

Locked-off camera, framing holds. The man in the brown suit leans into the wooden wheelbarrow of paper bundles and rolls it slowly forward a short way, then stops, the heap staying put. His mask, gloves and suit stay unchanged. The vault door and bulb stay still. SFX: a creaking wheel, a thud as each bundle lands, a low hum from the bulb. No voices.

Locked-off camera, framing holds, no camera movement. The man on the ledge shuffles one small step sideways along the ledge, back flat to the wall, then freezes. The sack in his hand sways once over the drop and settles. The tiny cars far below creep slowly along the street in their lanes. Mask, gloves and suit stay exactly as they are. SFX: high wind gusting, a shoe scraping stone, faint distant car horns. No voices, no music.

Locked-off camera, no zoom, pan or tilt; one continuous shot. The big gloved hand in the foreground stays up, fingers spread, never passing over his face: on each beat it wiggles its fingers like a stage magician, then snaps them, then waves slowly side to side. Behind his back, in plain view, his other hand keeps slowly pushing the folded banknote deeper into his jacket pocket until it is gone inside. His head stays where it is, tilted showily, facing the lens. His mask stays exactly as in the first frame: white ring, one red triangle, no holes. Smoke drifts in the spotlight. A finger snap, cloth rustle.

Locked-off camera, framing holds. The six masked men perform at the lens from the first frame and never stop, all bouncing at the knees together on every beat. First beat: CRIMSON jabs his finger at the lens twice. Next: PLUM and BOTTLE chop gloved palms down in unison. Next: MARINE and RUST lean in over Crimson's shoulders, fists pumping. Next: SILVER spreads both arms wide, palms down. Then all six chop down together and Crimson jabs again. Masks, suits, gloves and the hat stay unchanged; the customers keep their hands up. SFX: stamping shoes on marble, cloth swishing, a quiet lobby echo.

Locked-off camera, framing holds. On the first beat all six chop their outstretched arms down hard and drop into a knee bounce together. On the next, RUST, nearest, jabs a finger straight at the lens; PLUM and BOTTLE lean in behind him, palms rocking side to side. CRIMSON nods deep on every downbeat. MARINE swings his arm up late and points; SILVER shrugs, palms up, then chops again. They never stop: a new move every beat, bouncing in their places. Masks, gloves and suits stay unchanged; dust drifts, the parked cars stay put. SFX: shoes scuffing dry crust, cloth swish, gloved claps, wind. No voices.

Locked-off camera looking down, framing holds. From the first beat the five on the jetty bounce together at the knees, gloved fingers jabbing up at the lens. On the next beat PLUM and SILVER chop flat palms down while CRIMSON and RUST lean in shoulder to shoulder; MARINE in the centre pushes his head up toward the lens, both arms wide. Next, all five pump index fingers up twice, then swap: two lean left, two right. Behind them BOTTLE keeps tying the rope, nodding hard on every beat. Six men, unchanged; boat and lantern still. SFX: boot stamps on wet boards, cloth rustle, water lapping. No voices.

Locked-off camera, framing holds. From the first half-second all six bounce together on the beat, knees flexing. On the first beat they snap gloved right hands up from the low chop and chop down again, SILVER now on time. Next beat CRIMSON leans into the lens and jabs a finger at it while PLUM and MARINE swing open palms toward us. Then RUST and SILVER pump fists at the lens and BOTTLE rocks his free hand, the lunch pail kept low. They keep trading moves, leaning in and out. Six men throughout; masks, triangles, gloves, suits and city unchanged. SFX: boot stamps on planks, cloth, wind, no voices.

Locked-off camera looking straight up, framing holds. From the first half second the six bounce on the beat and stab their gloved fingers down at the lens. On the first beat PLUM and SILVER jab together; on the next BOTTLE and CRIMSON lean in, heads dipping toward the lens; then MARINE chops a flat palm down while RUST pumps his pointing hand twice. Every man keeps a fresh move each beat, shoulders dropping on the downbeat, all six the same size. The airship hangs still, the binoculars swing on their strap. Masks, gloves and suits unchanged. SFX: gloved claps, cloth rustle, high wind.

Locked-off camera, framing holds. From the first frame the six masked men bounce together on the beat and keep moving. First beat: CRIMSON, hunched low, stabs his finger at the lens. Next: MARINE slaps his raised glove down onto the crown of Crimson's hat and pulls it away again. Next: PLUM and BOTTLE swing their fists forward together. Next: RUST and SILVER chop flat palms down twice. Then all six nod hard on the same beat and Crimson points again. Behind the brass bars the clerk keeps counting notes. Masks, suits and gloves stay unchanged. SFX: shoe stamps, cloth, a big hall echo.

Locked-off camera, framing holds. The raised fists punch down on the first beat, every man landing a heel bounce on the ice together. On the next, SILVER, nearest, leans into the lens and jabs a finger at it; PLUM and MARINE chop flat palms down beside him. CRIMSON pumps his fist back up; RUST and BOTTLE, at the far end, rock palms side to side, shoulders dropping on each beat. Then all six throw fists high again, still bouncing. Masks, gloves and suits stay unchanged; snow keeps falling through the headlamp beams, the sedans stay still. SFX: boots crunching snow, cloth, wind, stamps on the beat. No voices.

Locked-off camera at eye level, framing holds. On the first beat the back row, CRIMSON, MARINE and SILVER, bounce with hands up, palms slapping down on each beat. PLUM, crouched front, snaps his spread arms in and jabs both index fingers at the lens; BOTTLE and RUST rock forward on their heels, chopping flat palms down in turn. On the next beats the back row lean in over the front row's shoulders, pointing at the lens, while PLUM spreads his arms wide again. The ground-crew man keeps hammering his peg. Balloon and ropes hold still. SFX: claps, mallet knocks, wet grass, cloth. No voices.

Locked-off camera, framing holds. From the first half-second CRIMSON, crouched at the front, jabs his finger at the lens on every beat, head pushed forward; on the third beat he sweeps the arm wide and jabs again. Behind him PLUM, BOTTLE, MARINE and SILVER bounce bent-kneed, chopping flat palms down on each beat, then all four swing their hands at the lens together, then back to chopping. RUST keeps polishing the propeller with his handkerchief, ignoring them. Propellers stay still, the plane stays parked. Six men throughout; masks, triangles, gloves and suits unchanged. SFX: feet thudding on dry grass, cloth, summer wind, no voices.

Locked-off camera down the aisle, framing holds. From the first half second the six bounce on the beat in their column. On the first beat MARINE's raised hand chops down flat toward the lens; on the next SILVER swings his gloved hand out and jabs a finger at the lens; then BOTTLE and PLUM lean out on opposite sides, arms swinging, while CRIMSON and RUST nod hard, shoulders dropping on each downbeat. A new move every beat, all six the same size. The steward stays put, tray of teacups perfectly level; countryside streams past the windows. Masks, gloves and suits unchanged. SFX: wheels clacking on rails, stamps, cloth.

Locked-off camera, framing holds. The six masked men keep moving from the first frame, knees bouncing together on every beat. First beat: CRIMSON, crouched nearest, pushes his flat palm at the lens and chops it down. Next: PLUM pumps his raised fist; BOTTLE points down at the lens. Next: MARINE and RUST swing their arms forward together. Next: SILVER flicks a banknote off his lapel, then points at the lens. Then all six chop down at once. The fire keeps burning gently in the doorway behind and banknotes drift slowly down. Masks, suits and gloves stay unchanged. SFX: crackling fire, shoes on stone, fluttering paper.

Locked-off camera, framing holds. On the first beat the five in the street drop deeper into their crouch and swing both arms at the lens, palms down. On the next, CRIMSON, centre, jabs two fingers straight at the camera; PLUM and BOTTLE chop palms down beside him; MARINE and SILVER rock their hands side to side, shoulders rolling. RUST, seated on the roadster's bonnet, waves his raised hand on the beat and points down at the lens. They keep bouncing, a new move each beat. Masks, gloves and suits stay unchanged; banknotes flutter down, the crowd cheers in place. SFX: shoes stamping, cloth, crowd murmur, paper rustle. No voices.

Locked-off camera low at the lens, framing holds. From the first beat PLUM, close in the foreground, jabs his gloved finger at the lens on every beat, his shoulders dipping and his masked head pushing in. Behind him CRIMSON, MARINE, RUST and SILVER pump their hands at the lens together, bouncing at the knees; on the third beat they all chop flat palms down at once, then point again. BOTTLE, at the back, bounces the umbrella up and down on the beat. All stay on their spots in the V. The marquee bulbs keep blazing, rain falls steadily. SFX: shoe stamps on wet cobbles, rain, cloth. No voices.

Locked-off camera, framing holds. From the first half-second PLUM, close at the front, jabs his gloved finger at the lens on each beat, pushing his head in. SILVER, front right, punches his fists toward us in turn. Behind them CRIMSON, MARINE and RUST bounce bent-kneed, pumping fists at the lens; on the fourth beat all five lean in together and chop palms down, then back to pumping. BOTTLE, at the back, holds the umbrella up and nods hard on every beat. Rain falls, puddles ripple, the marquee glows steadily. Six men throughout; masks, triangles, gloves and coats unchanged. SFX: rain on cobbles and umbrella, boot stamps, cloth, no voices.

Locked-off camera looking down from the ladder, framing holds. From the first half second the five in the cluster bounce on the beat, heads tipped up. On the first beat RUST snaps his pocket watch shut and keeps it in his fist; on the next he strides two steps in beside SILVER and pumps that fist at the lens. Meanwhile PLUM and CRIMSON jab fingers up on alternate beats, BOTTLE punches his fist upward, MARINE chops a flat palm, SILVER waves his open hand side to side. All six stay the same size. Masks, gloves and suits unchanged. SFX: shoes stamping on tar, gloved claps, distant city.

From the first frame the six men keep walking down the steps toward the camera at one steady, unhurried pace, one step per beat, arms loose, heads level, nobody looks back. Behind them the orange fireball keeps rolling slowly upward and fades to smoke. A few blank paper notes flutter down and settle on the steps. The paper in the left man's glove keeps burning gently. Locked-off camera, framing holds; masks, suits and gloves stay exactly as they are. SFX: a deep low rumble, crackling fire, footsteps on stone. No speech, no music.

From the first frame the six men keep walking straight at the lens in their V formation, one stride per beat, open overcoats flaring behind them. The grey-masked man tugs his cuff straight once; the man on the far right glances down at his pocket watch, then snaps it shut. Nobody turns his head. The marquee bulbs keep chasing; rain glints on the cobbles. Long-lens compression, so they grow only slightly larger. Locked-off camera, framing holds; masks, suits and gloves unchanged. SFX: heavy footsteps on wet stone, light rain, a faint electric hum. No speech, no music.

Locked-off camera, framing holds. The wooden speedboat on the left keeps leaping through its wake, bow high, then drops and slaps back onto the water in a wide fan of white spray. The man in the stern foreground holds his point at the horizon, dead still, and lowers his chin to glance at the pocket watch in his other hand. The searchlight beam stays fixed. Wardrobe and crates unchanged. SFX: engine snarl, a heavy splash, wind and spray.

Locked-off long-lens side view, framing holds. The steam train rolls steadily toward the left across the trestle, smoke pouring back over the carriages. On the roof the two men keep sprinting toward the right in long strides, cash sacks swinging, and the two hats tumble away behind them on the wind and drift out of the top of the frame. The man on the right keeps his sarcastic point at the camera. SFX: chugging engine, rattling rails, a steam whistle, wind.

Locked-off camera, framing holds. From the first frame the cream roadster rolls slowly forward toward the lower left and stays fully in frame. The standing man keeps flinging fistfuls of notes from the sack in a steady rhythm, his raised arm pumping. The notes flutter and drift down onto the crowd, who snatch at them. The driver stays still, hands on the wheel. Same car, same masks and gloves throughout; no one new appears. SFX: idling engine, crowd cheering, paper rustling.

Locked-off camera, high angle holds. From the first frame the bare bulb swings hard on its flex, its hard shadows sweeping across the tiled floor and crates. All five men stay frozen, arms locked, dead serious. On the second second, all five drop their thumbs at the same instant like a pistol hammer, and the man with the banana does the same, then they hold perfectly still. Smoke drifts in the beam. Masks and gloves unchanged; no one else enters. SFX: creaking flex, five tiny clicks in unison, low hum.

Locked-off camera, framing holds. From the first frame the man keeps firing the prop drum-magazine submachine gun straight up at the hanging globe lamps, braced wide, the barrel staying pointed upward. Bright flashes at the muzzle, small recoil in his shoulders. Each lamp he aims at bursts into falling glass, sparks drop and die out, and the near end of the hall grows darker while the far lamps glow. Plaster dust drifts. Mask, hat and gloves unchanged; no one else appears. SFX: rapid rattling bursts, glass shattering, echo in the marble hall.

High on the steel beam, the six men pass the lunch along the row. The man in the pinstripe suit, third from left, hands his sandwich with a banknote poking out to the man in the cream suit beside him, who takes it and gives it a slow, approving look. The others sit calmly, legs swinging gently over the drop. Locked-off camera, framing holds, all six stay seated, masks and suits unchanged. SFX: wind at height, distant riveting, far-off city hum.

The speedboat holds its place in frame, cutting forward through flat water. The man on the right tips the wooden crate further over the stern and a steady slab of banknotes slides out, the notes fluttering down onto the churning wake and floating away behind. The man on the left holds up his single note, glances at it, and flicks it after the rest. The distant patrol boat stays tiny on the horizon. Locked-off camera, framing holds. SFX: engine drone, hissing wake, paper flutter.

The elevated train rolls steadily on round the curve, the car swaying gently. The man on the outside step holds the brass grab rail, his body leaning out with the sway, the cash bag swinging in a slow arc over the drop and his white tie fluttering in the wind. In the window, the commuter keeps reading and holds the ticket out, never looking up. The trestle girders and sunlight stripes slide past steadily. Locked-off camera on the train, framing holds. SFX: clattering wheels, rattling steel, wind.

From the first frame the man in the cream suit slides steadily down the single rope, hand under hand, legs together, shoes pointed, dropping smoothly toward the deck at an unhurried pace. The five men on the deck stand completely still, hands in pockets, watching him. The blimp holds its place at the mast and the city lights glow steady below. Masks, gloves and suits unchanged; no one new appears. Locked-off camera, framing holds. SFX: rope creak, high wind, a distant ship horn.

From the first frame the clerk at the press freezes mid-turn, then slowly raises both hands beside his head, stiff with alarm. Through the round vault doorway the two masked men stand completely still, upright prop guns pointing at the ceiling, as if posing, the shelves behind them bare. The vault door, press and stack of green paper stay exactly where they are. Masks, gloves and suits unchanged; no one new appears. Locked-off camera, framing holds. SFX: lamp hum, a slow metal creak from the door.

Slow motion from the first frame. The man in cream keeps sinking backwards under the lowest thread, raised leg sweeping slowly over it, arms gliding wide, jacket hem drifting. Behind him the man in tweed keeps strolling straight forward at an even pace, the threads pulling taut against his chest and the little bells swinging. Masks, gloves and suits stay exactly the same. Locked-off camera, framing holds. SFX: tiny brass bells tinkling, soft footsteps, low hum of the bulb.

From the first frame the two crouching men tug the shared pliers back and forth between them in short jerks, their free gloved hands jabbing at different wires. The standing man above stays perfectly still and bored, one gloved finger resting on the clock's bell. The dynamite, clock and wires stay fixed to the safe door. Masks, hats and gloves stay exactly the same. Locked-off camera, framing holds. SFX: loud clock ticking, pliers clinking, cloth rustling.

From the first frame the round slab of floor with the two seated men lowers slowly and steadily straight down toward the lens, perfectly level, as plaster dust and paint flakes keep falling through the shaft of daylight. The two men stay seated with legs crossed; the man on the right gives his cuff one small tug. Masks, suits and gloves stay exactly the same; the vault walls stay still. Locked-off camera looking up. SFX: creaking timber, trickling plaster, soft rumble.

From the first frame the bright spark races along the fuse across the sunburst floor toward the black safe on the right, scattering small sparks that drop and die out. The six crouching men stay crouched in their arc, puffing their cigars, smoke curling upward; nobody hurries. The cake on the safe stays still. Masks, hats, suits and gloves stay exactly the same. Locked-off camera, framing holds. SFX: hissing fizzing fuse, soft puffs of cigar smoke, distant ticking clock.

Locked-off camera, framing holds. The masked man performs from the first instant, head bobbing hard on every beat. On the first beat his pointing finger jabs at the lens twice, sharp. On the next he snaps the hand back and chops it flat down through the air. Then a huge sarcastic shrug, both palms up, head cocked. Then he leans in and jabs at the lens again. The porter keeps slowly pushing his loaded cart, staying in frame. Mask, hat, gloves and suit unchanged; no new objects. SFX: leather glove creaks, cloth swishes, cart wheels, echoing station hall.

Locked-off camera, framing holds. The crouching man in the hat moves from the first instant: he taps both temples twice on the beat, then flings both hands open toward the lens, then bobs on bent knees, tapping again, feet planted on the beam. Behind him the four standing men nod together on each beat; the seated man holds his sandwich still against his mask and stares. Everyone stays on the girder. Masks, gloves and suits unchanged; nothing new appears. SFX: wind gusting, steel creaking, distant city traffic far below.

Locked-off camera, framing holds. The six masked men perform in unison to the lens on a fast beat from the first instant. First beat: the five raised arms chop down to point at the lens together; the man in the mustard mask finally throws his arm straight up, alone. Next beat: he snaps it down, late again. Next: all six bounce on bent knees and roll their shoulders. Next: all six fling both arms out wide. The band keeps playing; the dancers sway in place. Masks, gloves and suits stay unchanged. SFX: brass band, stamps on the stage, applause.

Locked-off camera, framing holds. The masked man moves from the first instant: from the shrug he drops both shoulders, then snaps them up again on the beat, palms up. On the next beat he swings one gloved hand to present the egg on the porter's tray, then counts off two fingers at the lens, then shrugs big again, head cocked. The porter stays still holding the tray level, egg in place, gazing at nothing. Fields stream past the windows. Mask, gloves and suit unchanged; nothing new appears. SFX: rails clacking, cutlery rattling softly.

Locked-off camera, framing holds. The six masked men in the ring perform at once from the first instant, staring up at the lens. On the first beat every raised fist pumps up twice in unison; the green-masked man in front is a beat late, his fist only reaching chest height. On the next beat they all bounce at the knees, heads nodding hard. Then all thump a fist to their chest together. Then every fist punches straight up again, green still late. Smoke drifts slowly through the window light. Masks, suits and gloves unchanged; nobody new appears. SFX: stamps on canvas, creaking ropes, cloth, echoing gym.

Locked-off camera, framing holds. From the first half-second he performs to the lens, foot staying on the crate: on the first beat his lower glove chops down flat, edge first; on the next he leans further over his knee toward the lens; then the chop again, harder; then he tugs his lapel with the other glove, chin lifting in mock pride; then a slow, smug head nod on the downbeat, and he repeats the chop. Head turns stay small; his mask and suit stay exactly as they are. The pigeon keeper keeps scattering grain, back turned. SFX: glove thumps, cloth rustle, pigeons cooing, distant city.

Locked-off camera, framing holds. From the first half-second the man raps with his whole body, knees bouncing on the beat, feet planted on the step. On the first beat his raised finger jabs up at the racing paper twice; on the next his other glove rubs the money sign hard at the lens; then both arms snap wide, palms down; then a big sarcastic shrug, palms up; then the finger jabs up again. Hands stay below and beside his masked face. The pressman keeps reading, bored. Mask, suit and gloves unchanged. SFX: rotary presses clattering, paper hissing.

Locked-off camera, framing holds. From the first instant the man raps with the microphone held tight to his masked mouth. On the first beat his spread glove snaps shut into a fist; on the next it bursts open again, a magician's flash; then the open hand sweeps slowly across in front of his chest, like a conjuror waving a cloth, and flings wide again. Knees bounce on every beat, torso dipping towards the lens. He keeps the microphone the whole time. The dancers keep kicking; the stagehand stands bored, holding his rope. Mask and gloves stay exactly as they are. SFX: tap of heels, cloth.

Locked-off camera, framing holds. Both men perform from the first half-second, sharp moves on the beat. The man on the left thrusts his flat palm at the lens twice, a hard stop sign, then wags one gloved finger side to side, then chops the palm down; his other glove keeps hold of the chrome microphone throughout. The man on the right keeps his hand cupped at his ear, leans further toward the brass horn, nods deeply on each beat and pops his shoulders. Behind the counter the shopkeeper keeps calmly winding the gramophone. Masks, hat, gloves and suits unchanged. SFX: gramophone crank, crackle, leather creak.

Locked-off camera, framing holds. From the first half-second the man raps with his body, leaning over the table, his left glove staying flat on the baize. On the first beat his open right hand sweeps grandly toward the dark doorway; on the next it jabs a finger at the lens; then he shrugs, palm up, head cocked; then a deep nod on the downbeat; then the presenting sweep again, too much, held. His masked face stays toward camera. The old man keeps chalking his cue, never looking up. Mask, suit and gloves unchanged. SFX: lamp hum, chalk squeak, balls clicking softly.

Locked-off camera, framing holds. From the first half-second all six wag their raised index fingers side to side in unison, on the beat, the fingers staying beside their heads, clear of the masks. The man at the back right lifts his finger late and joins in. On the fourth beat they all stop together, snap the finger down to point at the lens, then give one slow, sarcastic head shake. Feet stay planted; heads turn only slightly; masks, hat and suits stay exactly as they are. The deckhand keeps coiling rope, ignoring them. SFX: gulls, water lapping, a ferry engine thrum, creaking deck.

Locked-off static camera, framing holds. The masked man slowly settles the mustard jacket over the old woman's shoulders and smooths it down with both gloved hands, then rests one hand on her shoulder and stays still. She shivers once and her breath leaves a small white cloud in the cold air. The frost on the window, the empty grate and the cup stay unchanged. SFX: quiet room tone, a thin wind against the glass, wool rustling. No voices.

Locked-off camera, no camera movement. From the first frame the masked man in the maroon suit raps to the lens, leaning in. On the first beat he wags his raised finger at camera, mock-stern; on the next he tips his head up to the sky, exasperated; then he mimes holding a dainty invisible slice of cake between thumb and finger, little finger out, raises it to chin height, stops dead, and shakes his head at the lens; then he slides the empty hand forward, offering it to the viewer, and wags the finger again. Mask stays exactly as it is; other hand stays on his hip.

Camera travels alongside the lead roadster, locked off, framing holds; the three 1920s roadsters keep their places while the cracked lake bed streaks past and the amber dust plumes billow behind. The masked driver nods on a steady beat, then lifts his right gloved hand from the wheel and points it into the lens, holds, and returns it to the wheel. His white tie whips back. Mask unchanged, no new vehicles. SFX: engines roaring, gravel spray, wind. No voices.

Locked-off camera, framing holds. The three masked men walk two slow steps toward camera through the blizzard, prop guns held straight up, then stop together. They nod heads and shoulders on a steady beat while their free gloved hands chop down in time. Snow streaks through the headlight beams. The parked sedans stay exactly where they are, nobody else appears, masks unchanged. SFX: howling wind, boots crunching on snow, idling engines. No voices.

Locked-off camera, framing holds, no camera movement. The man crouching on the roof lets go of the sack; it drops once into the raised hands of the man below, who catches it and pulls it to his chest. The two men standing on the roof pump their raised fists up on the beat, heads nodding. Steam rolls slowly; the train, car and headlights stay where they are. SFX: hissing steam, a thud as the sack is caught. No voices, no music.

Locked-off camera, framing holds, the speedboat stays in the same place in frame as the dark water rushes past beneath it. White spray fans from the hull and falls back to the water. The searchlight beam from the left stays steady on the boat. The driver keeps both hands on the wheel; the kneeling man holds the drum-magazine prop still, pointed at the sky. The masks, the tarp and the crates stay unchanged. Audio: SFX of a roaring engine and slapping spray, wind.

Locked-off high camera, framing holds. The policemen bring their axes down into the oak barrels once each, and amber liquor gushes out and spreads slowly across the plank floor around the cards and chairs. The masked man carrying the crate walks steadily toward the open back door on the right. The masked man in the red suit holds the door still. The masks and the room stay unchanged. Audio: SFX of splitting wood, gushing liquid, heavy boots on boards.

Slow motion, locked camera; no zoom, pan or tilt. He keeps flying sideways through the air, travelling only a little to the right and sinking slightly as gravity takes him, his cream jacket flapping and his trouser legs rippling. He holds the gun pointed straight up at the ceiling in both gloved hands the whole time. His head stays square to the lens and large in frame. Behind him glass crystals fall steadily, glint in the window light and bounce off the marble counter. The mask stays exactly as it is: white ring, red triangle, no holes. Tinkling glass, cloth snapping. No speech.

Locked-off camera, tripod-stable, no zoom, pan or tilt; one continuous shot. The man stands still in the window frame of the fallen house front. At once his gloved hand brushes the dust off his lapel in two firm strokes, then he squares his shoulders, tugs his jacket straight with one hand and sets his feet, the carpet bag held steady at his side. A last puff of plaster dust settles round his boots. His head stays square to the lens throughout; his knitted mask does not change. Sound: settling timber creaks, a cloth brush, a distant dog.

Locked-off camera, tripod-stable, no zoom, pan or tilt; one continuous shot. The man leans on the standing barrel with both gloved hands flat on its rim. Whiskey keeps glugging from the split barrel at his feet and spreads slowly across the cobbles in a widening amber puddle. He straightens his back, plants both hands on the barrel lid and gives it one firm, heavy pat, then rests there, deadpan. His head stays still, angled down at the spill; his knitted mask does not change. Sound: liquid gurgling, a dull wooden thump.

Locked-off camera, tripod-stable, no zoom, pan or tilt; one continuous shot. The two men hold the canvas sack between them over the basket rim and give it two hard, shared shakes, so a thick stream of banknotes tumbles out and flutters away down towards the clouds. On the third beat they lift the empty sack and hold it out flat, deadpan, facing the lens. Their heads stay square to the camera and do not turn; both knitted masks stay exactly as they are. The ropes sway a little. Sound: wind, flapping paper, creaking wicker.

Camera locked to the car's bonnet, no zoom, pan or tilt; one continuous shot. The car swerves hard down the street from the first moment. The driver in the crimson mask and hat yanks the wheel left, then right, on the beat, shoulders and elbows heaving. The man in the cream suit beside him slams both gloved hands flat on the dashboard and braces, chest rocking with each swerve. Both heads stay square to the lens. Masks stay exactly as in the first frame: white ring, one small red triangle high on the right of each face, no holes. Oranges keep falling; the policeman stumbles clear. Engine roar, tyres squeal.

Locked-off camera, framing holds, moving with the plane. The man on the ladder sways gently in the wind, gripping the rung. He lifts the canvas cash bag up to chest height and gives it one slow, cocky shake towards the lens, then lets it drop back to hang at his side and settles, swaying. His jacket flaps steadily; the fields below drift slowly backwards. His knitted mask, gloves and suit stay exactly as they are, his head facing the lens throughout. SFX: engine drone, rushing wind, creaking rope.

Locked-off tripod camera, the framing holds. One action only: a fourth bullet punches through the upper door panel, opening a new small hole; a hard shaft of daylight snaps through it into the dusty dark, and a short puff of pale wood splinters spits from the hole towards the lens and falls. The man flinches once, pressing flatter to the wall, gun kept upright, then stays still. Dust drifts slowly through the four light beams to the end. His knitted mask, hat and gloves stay exactly as they are; nothing new enters. SFX: one sharp wooden crack, splinters pattering, then a low room hum.

Locked-off camera, no zoom, pan or tilt; one continuous shot. The two men stand upright either side of the safe, heads facing the lens. On the first beat the man in the mustard suit raps the safe's top twice with his gloved knuckles; on the next he pats it like a prize horse; then his free hand points down at it and back to his own chest. The man in brown tweed rocks the sack truck a little on its wheels, the safe tilting, and nods on the beat. Masks stay exactly as in the first frame: white ring, one red triangle, no holes. Bulb sways slightly; knocks on iron.
